scope: Final visible Draft, exact source/article/action/deployed bytes, core native-dispatch 0.4.1-0.4.5 package and allowlist state, core #600/#608/#609/#612/#614-#619/#590/#597/#598/#602, BookcaseDiscovery #101-#103, daily-logger #548/#549/#550/#551/#552 and all open review-data PRs, workstation-yuri #11, current review schema/discovery, and held-candidate custody. Read-only review; no article revision or acceptance, finding disposition, action admission or settlement, readiness, merge, workflow dispatch, runtime, or scheduling authority.

findings.title: The repository and PR totals contradict the article inventory
findings.location: Lines 6, 11, 15-17 and 32-43 say twelve PRs across core and BookcaseDiscovery and seven core PRs while listing eight core, three BookcaseDiscovery and one daily-logger PR.
findings.explanation: Eight cited core PRs and three BookcaseDiscovery PRs merged in the window. Twelve is reached only by also including daily-logger #550 as a third repository.
findings.correction: Report eight core plus three BookcaseDiscovery merges, or twelve total only when daily-logger #550 is included as a third repository.

findings.title: The native-dispatch release and active allowlist profile are stale
findings.location: Lines 3, 11, 17, 49-57 and 81 call the merged state 0.4.3 and say the active authority is the four-plugin 2.1.308 profile.
findings.explanation: Pinned core package state is 0.4.5. Its shipped allowlist contains only isolated 2.1.286 with empty built-in lists; the old nonempty 2.1.286 and 2.1.308 traces are historical and cannot authorize the changed invocation.
findings.correction: Distinguish historical 0.4.3 / 2.1.308 qualification from final merged 0.4.5 state and name isolated 2.1.286 as the only active profile at the reviewed pin.

findings.title: The paired ledger links target the wrong repositories
findings.location: Line 17 sends BookcaseDiscovery #103 to core #103; line 34 sends core #618 to BookcaseDiscovery #618.
findings.explanation: The actual matched pair is core #618 and BookcaseDiscovery #103.
findings.correction: Link core #618 to ojfbot/core and BookcaseDiscovery #103 to ojfbot/BookcaseDiscovery.

findings.title: The catalog-v2 recovery range omits the highest measured set
findings.location: Lines 34 and 75 summarize v2 acceptance of v1 no-catalog-match boxes as 15-20% depending on set.
findings.explanation: BookcaseDiscovery #102 reports six point estimates from 15.8% through 23.9%; the held-out sf-store-005 every-10 set is 23.9% with a 21.6-26.3 interval. These remain machine-agreement measurements, not accuracy.
findings.correction: Report 15.8-23.9% across the six sets, retain per-set intervals and the machine-agreement limitation, and do not omit the held-out high value.

findings.title: Core #600 already records completed live replay evidence
findings.location: Line 91 labels core #600 source-review only and native-admission gated.
findings.explanation: PR #600 adds the operator-run command, reports an author-run live request plus duplicate and a separate Yojimbo replay, and states no blocking findings remain. It is still Draft/unmerged with no deployment or authority change, which are separate facts.
findings.correction: Describe #600 as an implemented Draft with completed author-reported and separate replay evidence, no blocking findings, and no deployment or delegated-authority change.

findings.title: Core #590 retains an explicit owner and ADR-acceptance gate
findings.location: Line 97 says core #590 has no reported blockers.
findings.explanation: The PR keeps owner review unchecked and requires acceptance to number the Proposed ADR with /adr accept and apply glossary terms.
findings.correction: Retain the explicit owner review and ADR-acceptance gate; green CI and non-Draft PR state do not remove it.

findings.title: The open review-data set and intended Draft lifecycle are misreported
findings.location: Line 101 says #551 plus nine earlier audits, lists only eight earlier PRs, omits five older open reviews and says none is designated for publication.
findings.explanation: Fourteen review-only Draft PRs were open: #515, #524, #526, #529, #530, #533, #535, #537, #539, #541, #543, #545, #547 and #551. The discovery service intentionally loads eligible open review-only PRs as proposed/current records pending supervised disposition.
findings.correction: Report all fourteen open review-data PRs and explain that Draft/open is their advisory proposed-publication state pending supervised finding disposition.

findings.title: Open non-Draft status does not establish readiness or a hidden blocker for #548/#549
findings.location: Lines 99 and 113-114 say no blocker is stated and propose identifying what holds each before either merging or naming the dependency.
findings.explanation: Both PRs are open/non-Draft with green observed checks, but neither has a public GitHub review or human merge authorization. #548 records an unenforced prompt-only disclosure rule as a known security limit. Silence establishes neither readiness nor a hidden blocker.
findings.correction: Report actual lifecycle, checks, absence of public review/merge authority and #548's known limit; request an owner decision without implying merge is the default.

findings.title: The combined three-step critical path to first live correspondence is not publicly established
findings.location: Lines 81-85 and retained draft context require #619 review-readiness, CG307-U1 admission and per-machine setup before any first live correspondence window.
findings.explanation: Core #619 is an unreleased standing-correspondence candidate. Core #618 and BookcaseDiscovery #103 record their own no-live-call and gated-admission boundaries, but do not publicly state that the ledger pair or standing candidate gates every one-off correspondence duty window. The retained context separately says #609 is not confirmed on the critical path.
findings.correction: Attribute only the gates each PR records and label the combined dependency chain unverified until a public owner or charter source binds it to the first live correspondence window.
